look_here_first: Small Central Texas canyon sedge with dense tufts, strongly purple-red culm bases, and a few widely separated spikes in dry-mesic calcareous woodland just above streams.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Cyperaceae/Carex: grasslike perennial sedges with sheathing leaves; Carex fruits are enclosed in a perigynium, a key structure for species-level identification.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: calcareous canyon and ravine woodland habitat

lookalikes.differences: C. edwardsiana often grows near C. planostachys. Look first for the purple-red culm bases, somewhat broader green blades, and more widely separated spikes; C. planostachys has narrower V-shaped/revolute leaves and a lower cedar-sedge look.
